clue.text: Rampage? Pat's wrapped up in it

explanation.surface: Someone goes on a rampage, and a man called Pat is bundled up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rampage' is split for a cryptic sense: a ram is something that butts, and a page is a sheet of paper. A pat of butter is a small slab, sold wrapped in greaseproof sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Read cryptically, ram-page is a butter (one that butts) plus a sheet; and the greaseproof wrapping round a pat of butter carries the same name.

clue.text: Film-crew or anything taken as one

explanation.surface: A film-crew regarded as a single body.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or camera crew is called a production team or squad; and any single whole counted as one is a single item.

clue.text: Carry a young child with ease at first

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word ease is wanted here

explanation.surface: Lifting and carrying a small child without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To lug or bear something along is a synonym for carry.

clue.text: Red rose embroidered in church tapestry…

indicators.note: embroidered suggests stitching a design, and here signals that the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A red rose stitched into a tapestry hanging in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is the ornamental screen or hanging behind a church altar, sometimes a tapestry.

clue.text: feature of a particular church

indicators.note: of says the answer is made of letters taken from inside the words particular church

explanation.surface: A characteristic feature of one particular church building.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from 4-down's ellipsis; the letters run across the join of 'particular' and 'church'.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved span over a doorway or nave is a typical architectural element of a church.

clue.text: Makes one see red as green changes?

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of as green are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Something that infuriates a person, as when a green traffic light switches.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to become furious, so making someone see red is to infuriate them.

clue.text: Live so hazardously and your legs collapse!

indicators.note: collapse suggests legs giving way, and here signals the letters falling into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning: live recklessly and your legs will give way under you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live so' prefaces the definition: to live this way is the familiar idiom for taking risks.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something hazardously means doing it with risk of harm.

clue.text: Formerly run Circle Line, without number being given

parts.note: ex- is the prefix meaning former
to run a business is to direct it
O is shaped like a circle
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Commentary on a London Underground route (the Circle Line) that used to be operated without its number being announced.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here 'Circle' and 'Line' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A British telephone subscriber who is unlisted has a number withheld from the public phone book.

clue.text: Chap getting a kiss from Douglas, perhaps?

parts.note: a chap is a man
X is written for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A man being kissed by somebody named Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is not a person but the capital of the Isle of Man; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a place on the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from the island in the Irish Sea whose capital is Douglas is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Imagine Jack, for example, in a suit

definitions.text: Imagine Jack, for example, in a suit

parts.words: Imagine Jack, for example, in a suit
parts.note: imagine suggests a mental image; a jack is one of the court cards in a pack, each belonging to a suit, and court cards carry a printed image

explanation.surface: Picture a man called Jack dressed up in a business suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack, queen and king of each suit are court cards bearing an illustrated figure.

clue.text: Hideous-sounding cross from the West Indies

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for hideous is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: hideous means ugly

explanation.surface: A nasty-sounding hybrid that comes from the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: This Jamaican citrus fruit is a hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine, so a cross.

clue.text: Jack's drawing theory?

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB (able seaman), plus the S of the possessive
traction is the act of drawing or pulling

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man named Jack's sketch illustrates some theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an abstract idea rather than something concrete.

clue.text: The volume turned up in the galley?

definitions.text: The volume turned up in the galley?

parts.words: The volume turned up in the galley?
parts.note: volume suggests loudness turned up, but means a book; a galley is a ship's kitchen, where a recipe book would be used

explanation.surface: Someone cranked up the sound in a ship's kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume of recipes is what a cook consults in a kitchen such as a galley.

clue.text: Flower to flourish outside vessel?

indicators.note: outside says the word for flourishing goes around the vessel's letters

parts.note: to bloom is to flourish
SS is a steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A flower growing well around the outside of a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit-tree flowers, en masse, are called by this name.

clue.text: Matched china with top of dresser

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, a friend

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word dresser

explanation.surface: Crockery paired with the uppermost shelf of a kitchen dresser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate) for a friend; a dresser is a kitchen cabinet with display shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: Things matched are paired up together.

clue.text: Judge to make mention of two points

parts.note: to refer to something is to mention it
E (east) is a compass point, taken twice

explanation.surface: A judge about to mention a pair of points in a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports umpire or arbitrator judges disputes.

clue.text: Android needs mainspring with bolt-head in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle places the bolt's first letter inside the word for a source

parts.note: the mainspring of something is its root or source
the head of bolt is its first letter, B

explanation.surface: A mechanical android requires a mainspring with a bolt fitted at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a humanlike automaton.

clue.text: Island of saint and prophet

parts.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: An island associated with a holy man and a prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean.

clue.text: Yorkshireman pretty keen to be seen inside

indicators.note: to be seen inside says the answer can be spotted within the words pretty keen

explanation.surface: A man from Yorkshire who is fairly eager to be seen indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a large county in northern England, whose people are nicknamed tykes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyke is a nickname, often affectionate, for a native of the county of Yorkshire.

clue.text: Match clubs, for example

explanation.surface: A game played with golf clubs, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fitting or harmonise is to match; and clubs is one of the four card categories, alongside hearts, diamonds and spades.

clue.text: Fabulous type striking a pose

indicators.note: striking a pose suggests adopting a stance, here it signals rearranging the letters of a pose

explanation.surface: A marvellous person adopting a posture for a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means wonderful in the surface, but here means writing fables.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author of fables is the classic teller of such tales.

clue.text: Not hear about the twelfth man?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of not hear are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone failing to hear news concerning the cricket team's reserve player.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the twelfth man is the substitute beyond the eleven players, so he is one more.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelfth man is an additional one beyond the eleven already counted.

clue.text: Hold out for price advance

parts.note: to advance a suggestion is to offer it

explanation.surface: Holding out for a better price on a cash advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out something to someone is to present it for acceptance.

clue.text: Silver ball on the beach

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a round is a spherical shape or bullet, a ball

explanation.surface: A silver ball lying on the sand by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the beach' suggests holidays, but means stranded on shore, as a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stuck on the beach is grounded, stranded on the shore.

clue.text: Toy right for the ne'er-do-well?

parts.note: to toy with something is to trifle with it

explanation.surface: A plaything for a good-for-nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frivolous who never does anything serious is a time-waster.

clue.text: Underground duct

explanation.surface: A subterranean pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: London's metro system is popularly known by this name; and a pipe or channel for fluid is a cylinder of the same name.

clue.text: Run down lodge?

explanation.surface: Running down to a country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock that has run down ceases to go; and to lodge somewhere is to stay there.

clue.text: Be jealous of ambassador having nothing to lose

indicators.note: to lose tells us the letter for nothing is dropped from the ambassador's word

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic ambassador
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Resenting an ambassador who has nothing more to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet what another has is to be jealous of them.

clue.text: Bones from Greek mountain

explanation.surface: Skeletal remains recovered from a mountain in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin plural of os, meaning bones, used in anatomy; and Mount Ossa is a peak in Thessaly piled on Pelion in Greek myth.

clue.text: Snap conclusion, of course

parts.note: a snap is a snapshot, a photo
a finish is a conclusion or end

explanation.surface: A hasty conclusion, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally', but means at a racecourse: the definition is a close race ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A race ending on the course so close that the result is judged from a camera image.

clue.text: Player giving lead on pitch?

parts.note: a player on a pitch suggests a footballer setting an example, but this is a musician giving the note an orchestra tunes to

explanation.surface: A footballer showing leadership on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: In an orchestra this woodwind instrument sounds the A to which the other players tune.

clue.text: Soames Forsyte as member of stage crew?

explanation.surface: Casting a Galsworthy character among theatre stagehands.
explanation.walkthrough: Soames Forsyte is the hero of Galsworthy's novel The Man of Property, the first part of The Forsyte Saga.
explanation.definitionFit: Galsworthy titled his novel about Soames after a man of possessions; and in a theatre, the stagehand in charge of props bears that title.
